messages:
support-alex: FYI incoming customer escalation — multiple customers reporting API timeouts and 5xx for hosted inference in us-west-2 since ~02:00 UTC. Example: cust_id=acme-331, request_id=req_0a1b2c3d. Support has a repro curl that intermittently hangs then 502s.

maria-sre: Paging oncall and runtime. Observability — any SLO burns showing for us-west-2? :eyes:

jordan-obs: Probe SLO alert fired at 02:14 UTC for gateway p99 latency > 1200ms, but probes look noisy and not matching real traffic. I'll pull dashboard and traces now.

kevin-runtime: I see a spike in backend worker queue length around 02:10–02:25 UTC on the hosted-infer pool. Many requests hit heavy-model-v2 which has longer tail. Possible KV cache churn?

oncall-bot: @maria-sre, @kevin-runtime — PagerDuty INC-8291 created (High severity).

maria-sre: Jordan — can you run these queries? 1) 5xx rate by route for us-west-2 2) p99 latency by route 3) trace coverage gap test. Paste results here.

jordan-obs: Running quick PromQL/BigQuery queries:```
# 5xx rate by route (prom)
sum(rate(api_http_responses_total{region="us-west-2",status=~"5.."}[5m])) by (route)

# p99 latency by route
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(api_request_duration_seconds_bucket{region="us-west-2"}[5m])) by (le, route))
```

jordan-obs: Results: majority of 5xx noise from /v1/infer and /v1/chat. p99 on /v1/infer jumped from 350ms -> 1.4s. Trace sampling rate dropped around the same time — trace coverage from 0.6 -> 0.12. There is a trace-gap for requests with large prompt sizes.

kevin-runtime: Could be the runner pool Autoscaler mis-evaluating load when many requests use long sequences. I’ll check the runner metrics and recent deploys.

deploy-bot: Rollout event: service/hosted-infer runners/v2 queued scaled to 0->8 at 01:58 UTC, health OK. New kernel patch rolled at 01:54 UTC.

maria-sre: @kevin-runtime prioritize: 1) confirm if kernel patch coincides with cache/eviction behavior 2) check if batching config changed 3) check per-model concurrency and per-worker memory OOMs. If we can repro, try repro with the customer's prompt payload.

support-alex: Customer supplied payload (redacted): prompt length ~ 18k tokens, use stream=false. They say it worked earlier today then degraded.

kevin-runtime: Running a local repro with same prompt. Observing KV-cache misses and long startup for the model, also occasional worker-level 502s with "upstream reset". Sending logs.```
[2026-03-12T02:11:23Z] runner-42 ERROR request=req_0a1b2c3d upstream reset during write
[2026-03-12T02:11:23Z] runner-42 WARN large-kv-cache-eviction: evicted 512MB
```

maria-sre: That looks like memory pressure causing connection resets. For mitigation: 1) enable canary fallback to lighter model variant for hosted inference routing policy 2) temporarily raise runner pool min size for us-west-2 3) re-enable prefix caching TTL to reduce cold starts. Can we execute those quickly?

kevin-runtime: I can raise min runners and flip routing to fallback in next 5 mins. Will also add a higher sampling rate for traces to capture repro paths.

jordan-obs: I'll patch the dashboard to show worker queue depth + KV eviction count & annotate the 01:54 kernel patch. Also running a trace-gap analysis to correlate customer request IDs.

support-alex: Customer on call at 02:40 UTC. I'll notify them of mitigation plan and ask for a few sample request_ids if more show up.

maria-sre: Good. After mitigation, we need a postmortem: root cause: heavy-model rollout + cache eviction + insufficient runner autoscale for long-sequence requests. Also ensure alerting covers trace-coverage drops (SLO-alert -> trace-gap correlation).

kevin-runtime: Mitigations applied: increased min runners to 12, toggled fallback routing for heavy-model-v2 -> heavy-model-v1. Early signals: 5xx rate decreasing, p99 falling back toward baseline. Monitoring closely. :thumbsup:

jordan-obs: Trace coverage back up to 0.55. Dashboard shows lower queue depth. Keeping retention on detailed traces for 24h.

maria-sre: Thanks team. Next steps: revert kernel patch in staging, add synthetic long-prompt probes to our probers, and add an alert that ties SLO burn to trace coverage < 0.3. I'll create action items in postmortem doc.

support-alex: Customer confirmed recovery at 03:05 UTC. I'll close the escalation after PM created. :white_check_mark:
